self-regulated learning, in the form of goal setting, has been shown to be effective for improving learning and performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
goal setting and self-regulation are important for students' academic achievement, and that self-efficacy is an important mediator of this relationship.

the more students are involved in the process of setting their own learning goals, and the more they are involved in the monitoring of their goal progress, the more likely they are to achieve their learning goals, and to be successful in the long run.
the more students are engaged in the learning process, the more likely they are to be successful in their learning and to transfer what they have learned to other situations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
goal setting is a powerful way for people to improve their performance.
goal setting and self-regulation are not only related to each other, but also interact with one another to affect academic outcomes.
goal setting is a powerful strategy for enhancing performance, and that the benefits of goal setting can be maximized by setting goals that are specific, challenging, and attainable.
